findings.claim: The landmark_00_local_dx coordinate proxy is non-monotone over the full observed window [0.0,0.49]: it rises from a near-zero start to a positive peak near t≈0.10-0.11, then falls to a negative trough near t≈0.19, and returns toward small positive values by the window end.

The observed-node linear fit for landmark_00_local_dx is not accepted (polynomial_accepted=false, relative_node_RMSE≈0.78), with 6 sign changes and 9 strong sign conflicts across 14 independent batches, so a single global linear trend is not supported for this feature.

The endpoint rate contrast for landmark_00_local_dx is strongly negative at the window start (first_rate_z≈-17.5) and positive at the window end (last_rate_z≈8.1), while the whole-window level contrast is small (whole_window_z≈-0.18); the sign of the local change therefore reverses across the window.

The learning window and observed score times span [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score nodes at 0.01 spacing, and recorded affinities were removed with an equal score prior; selection preference is therefore association evidence, not measured final affinity.

hypotheses.direction: non-stationary; early negative rate, late positive rate
hypotheses.falsifier: A refit on the same support showing no sign reversal in the local rate, or a stable accepted polynomial with no strong sign conflicts, would falsify this.
hypotheses.statement: A time-varying (non-stationary) contrast in landmark_00_local_dx is supported over the observed window: the local rate is negative early and positive late, so a single stationary target for this coordinate proxy is not supported by the observed curve.

hypotheses.falsifier: Evidence that the whole-window level contrast dominates and the rate reversal is within batch noise would falsify this.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_local_dx whole-window level vs endpoint rate
hypotheses.statement: Because the whole-window level contrast for landmark_00_local_dx is small while the endpoint rate contrast reverses sign, any reward term keyed to this coordinate should be evaluated against a changing contrast rather than a fixed absolute target.

limitations: Only one coordinate proxy curve (landmark_00_local_dx) was read; other landmark coordinates were not queried, so cross-coordinate consistency is unobserved.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; no stage boundary is inferred.
The curve is a predicted endpoint world-A coordinate proxy; no energy, chemical-interaction, or neural-module interpretation is attached.
Selection preference is association evidence only; descendant survival and decoded final affinity are not observed here.
The observed-node linear fit was not accepted and shows strong sign conflicts, so the reported trend is descriptive of the observed window and not an extrapolatable law.
